When typing a letter with a diacritic, does the typist expect to press the diacritic key before the letter, or type the letter first and then the diacritic?

For example: pressing the diacritic key first and then the letter (like pressing a key for an acute accent and then a to get a-with-acute, or pressing an underdot key before s to get s-with-underdot), or typing the letter first and then a suffix key (like typing a and then a special key to add the diacritic after). There is no wrong answer -- this depends on what feels natural to your community and what existing keyboards already do.

Diacritic key first, then the letter (the diacritic key is pressed before the base letter)
Letter first, then the diacritic key (type the base letter, then press a key to add the diacritic)

stations.textBefore:
When a letter with a mark is written, what should your keyboard send?

From the previous question — you type the letter first, then its mark.

You type the letter first and then its mark, so we suggest your keyboard sends the letter and the mark as separate characters, in the order they were typed. You can choose single ready-made characters instead — when the mark is typed, your keyboard can replace the letter with the single character.

Send the letter and its mark as separate characters
(suggested)
á — U+0061 + U+0301 (separate characters)
Backspace clears the mark first and the plain letter next, and searching or comparing text matches the letter as a letter followed by its mark.
Send each accented letter as one single ready-made character
á — U+00E1 (one character)
Backspace clears the whole accented letter in one press, and searching or comparing text matches the letter as a single unit.
What should backspace do to an accented letter?

Your keyboard sends the letter and its mark as separate characters, so a backspace press can take the mark off first — we suggest backspace removes one mark at a time. You can choose the whole letter at once instead: your keyboard can add the extra rules that clear a letter and all its marks in a single press.

Backspace removes one mark at a time (letter and mark kept separate)
recommended
Backspace removes the whole letter at once (one ready-made unit)

GETTING STARTED · DESKTOP

Welcome to the Mechanism Gallery

This is where you build your keyboard. For each character your language needs that the starting keyboard doesn’t already have, you’ll choose how to type it on a desktop keyboard.

You’ll go character by character through the list from your survey.
Pick a method — use a dead key, swap a key, or use AltGr — or mark a character for later review if you’d rather come back to it.
Need several keystrokes for one character? Pick “Type a sequence” and a small builder opens right here, in place of the preview.
Phones and tablets come later, in the Touch gallery.
